answer: DeepWalk’s largest reported gains are on sparse, low-label-rate settings—especially when only a small fraction of nodes are labeled for training. In the original experiments, its advantage over competing methods was biggest on the more challenging datasets and at the lowest training-label percentages, where it could substantially outperform methods that rely more heavily on labeled data or hand-engineered features.
